subject: Segregated networking & air-gapped constraints — RFI response and next steps
messages:
From: Peter Holdsworth <peter.holdsworth@stargatehealth.com>

Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI — networking segregation & air-gapped constraints

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. As part of our internal security RFI for private deployments, we need a focused response on networking and air-gap constraints. High level items we need clarified:

- Can Redwood support a completely air-gapped on-prem deployment with no outbound NAT? If partial outbound is required, what minimal services are needed (DNS, NTP, CRL/OCSP, update channels)?
- Does the private control plane require connectivity to Redwood HQ for management/telemetry? If so, can that be disabled and replaced with a customer-managed control plane?
- For VPC deployments: support for isolated subnets, egress restrictions, and routing with transit gateways/VPN — any limitations?
- Where do secret materials (model weights, keys) reside during install and runtime? KMS/HSM integrations?
- Evidence we can include in our packet (network diagrams, attestation letter, install-runbook snippets).

Can you provide a matrix and sample artifacts? Procurement would like the packet by EOW (Friday).

Thanks,
Peter
Peter Holdsworth
Head of IT Security — Stargate Health

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
To: Peter Holdsworth <peter.holdsworth@stargatehealth.com>
Cc: procurement@stargatehealth.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 13:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI — networking segregation & air-gapped constraints

Hi Peter — thanks for the clear list. We can accommodate a range of deployment postures; attaching an initial matrix that maps each ask to our current options and the required trade-offs. High level answers below and please see attachments for diagrams and snippets: redwood-segregated-networking-matrix.xlsx, airgap-deployment-guide.pdf.

- Air-gapped install: Supported. We provide an offline installer bundle (tar) that contains runtime, model artifacts, and installer scripts. No outbound NAT is required to run inference after installation. For update/patching we can supply an offline update process.
- Minimal external services: during initial provisioning you may optionally resolve an internal package repository. For continuous operation, DNS is not strictly required if IPs are fixed; NTP is recommended but can be provided via an internal NTP server; CRL/OCSP checks for client certs can be muted if using long-lived cert lifecycles — we document the security tradeoffs in the guide.
- Control plane: Our hosted control plane is optional. Customers may choose the Redwood Private control plane deployed inside their VPC or an entirely customer-managed control plane (we provide Helm charts and Terraform for this path). Telemetry can be routed to customer endpoints only; by default no telemetry leaves the customer network unless explicitly enabled.
- VPC feature set: support for isolated subnets, strict egress ACLs, transit gateway and VPN attachments are supported; we provide examples for route tables and NAT-less setups.
- Secrets: model weights and keys remain on customer storage (S3-compatible or NFS) for private installs. KMS integrations: AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM via PKCS#11 are supported; runtime can be configured to fetch keys only from in-network KMS with no external delegation.

I'll loop in Monica (security) and Hiro (solutions) for the attestation and runbook snippets. We'll aim to deliver the full packet by Friday EOD.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Monica / Jasmine — here are the snippets for inclusion. I tested these in our internal air-gap lab last month.

1) Installer checksum verification (example, offline):
-----BEGIN SNIPPET-----
#!/bin/bash
TARFILE=redwood-offline-bundle.tar.gz
CHECKSUM_FILE=redwood-offline-bundle.sha256
sha256sum -c ${CHECKSUM_FILE} || { echo 'checksum mismatch'; exit 1; }
# extract and verify contents
-----END SNIPPET-----

2) systemd unit (model service):
-----BEGIN SNIPPET-----
[Unit]
Description=Redwood Inference Runtime - offline
After=network.target

[Service]
Type=simple
ExecStart=/opt/redwood/runtime/bin/redwood-runtime --config /etc/redwood/config.yml --no-telemetry
Restart=on-failure
User=redwood

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
-----END SNIPPET-----

3) Checksum/manifest: we include a signed manifest (SHA256 + RSA2048) with every offline bundle. Instructions to verify are in the guide.

I'll hand the artifacts off to Monica to produce the attestation PDF.

—Hiro
Hiro Tanaka
